A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Omni-Weather study. Their text, equations, six tables, twelve figures, and Appendices A.1–A.8 support reliable comparison. The appendix content matches after accounting for shifted pagination.

before.justification: v1 reports original radar generation and understanding experiments in Table 1, training and reasoning ablations in Tables 2–3, and additional encoder, data-mixing, and guidance experiments in Appendix A.6.

after.justification: v3 retains these original quantitative experiments and qualitative model outputs, including the appendix ablations. Results retained from v1 still constitute original empirical results.

M1.justification: The Bagel-7B-MoT backbone, EarthFormer radar sequence encoder, modality-specific encoders and decoders, joint training objective, and CoT construction and inference procedures remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix A.4.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same SEVIR nowcasting and satellite-to-radar inversion tasks, RadarQA frame and sequence understanding tasks, and general-data mixing experiments. No dataset, population, or evaluated task scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Earthformer, Diffcast, and Cascast for nowcasting; UNet, ViT, and WeatherGFM for inversion; and Claude-sonnet-4, Gemini-2.5-pro, GPT-5, and RadarQA for understanding. The comparator configurations in the main-text and appendix ablations also match.

E3.justification: Reported settings remain unchanged: ten input and twelve output nowcasting frames, 256×256 images, 20k training steps on eight H200 GPUs, the same evaluation metrics, and the same 200-example ablation evaluations. No new evaluation protocol is introduced.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 and Appendices A.5–A.7 retain the same joint-training, general-data mixing, CoT, encoder, and classifier-free guidance analyses and qualitative cases. Moving Figures 6–7 does not add an analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the model comparisons. Statistical and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 and the plotted and qualitative results match. For example, Table 1 retains nowcasting CSI-M values of 0.384 and 0.353 and LPIPS values of 0.179 and 0.166 for Omni-Weather without and with thinking, respectively. The appendix result entries are unchanged.

T1.justification: The task mapping, model formulation, and joint loss in Equations 3.1–3.4 are unchanged, as are the metric definitions in Appendix A.3. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The conclusion adds benefits concerning easier auditing and debugging and prospective broader task transfer and scalable evaluation. The abstract and introduction retain the central claims about unified generation and understanding, mutual task benefits, and CoT-enhanced perceptual quality.

C2.justification: v3 adds a specific limitation that reasoning traces may be imperfect and need stronger alignment with generated or predicted fields. Its new ethics statement also specifies research use with professional interpretation. v1's VAE and broader-validation limitations and the existing accuracy–perceptual-quality interpretation remain.

D1.justification: The new reproducibility statement identifies a dedicated CoT dataset and construction-code location and promises the complete codebase, checkpoints, and processing scripts upon acceptance. Existing implementation details and the abstract's public GitHub availability statement remain. This changes access documentation; the PDFs do not establish actual resource availability.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the bibliography add Cao et al. (2024) on scientific video diffusion and Cao et al. (2025) on domain prompt learning, while removing Xin et al. (2025), Lumina-DiMOO. The overall positioning around unified multimodal weather modeling is retained.

P1.justification: v3 retitles the paper around weather radar, replaces the Preprint header with an ICLR 2026 publication header, makes limited related-work and conclusion edits, and adds ethics/reproducibility and acknowledgments sections. Most prose, including the appendix, remains unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 6–7 move from page 9 to page 10, and surrounding text, references, and section breaks reflow. All figures and tables are retained without substantive redesign; the appendix body layouts match apart from headers and pagination.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves qualification of its reasoning claims by explicitly acknowledging faithfulness limitations and specifying expert oversight. Added CoT access documentation also helps readers locate resources. The scientific evidence remains unchanged, and the new future-release wording leaves availability ambiguous alongside the retained public-release statement, limiting the overall gain.
